title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
intro: This playbook consolidates our standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding, integration steps, escalation handling, known issues and workarounds, and quarterly business review (QBR) / health-check templates. It is intended for Customer Success, Support, Solutions Engineering, and Partner engineers working on Redwood Inference enterprise accounts.
audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Technical Account Managers (TAMs), and Engineering on-call leads.
objectives:
- Reduce time-to-production for enterprise customers.
- Provide a clear escalation path for sev1/sev2 incidents.
- Standardize integration checks and acceptance criteria.
- Capture known issues and deterministic workarounds to shorten MTTR.
- Provide a reusable QBR & health-check template for customer reviews.
prerequisites:
- Signed contract and account provisioning completed (billing and enterprise account flagged).
- Customer has an account in the Redwood Console with project and API keys provisioned.
- Networking information (VPC peering or IP allowlist) exchanged where applicable.
- Points of contact (POC), technical and business contacts provided by customer.
- Solutions Engineering onboarding task assigned in JIRA (tag: ENT-ONBOARD).
onboarding_checklist:
1) Kickoff & discovery (owner: CSM/Solutions Eng)
   - Schedule 60–90 minute kickoff within 5 business days of contract signature.
   - Discuss success metrics, uptime/latency SLOs, throughput expectations, and data residency requirements.

2) Accounts & Access (owner: Customer Success)
   - Create project(s) in Redwood Console; provision API keys and role-based access (IAM role: enterprise-customer).
   - Exchange SSH/KMS credentials for Private deployments if required (follow security-and-compliance/key-exchange checklist).

3) Network & Security (owner: Solutions Eng / Customer)
   - Verify VPC peering, IP allowlisting, or proxy configuration.
   - Confirm audit logging and retention policy for customer (default: 90 days; enterprise add-on available).

4) Integration & Test Plan (owner: Solutions Eng)
   - Provide quickstart sample app and SDK example matched to customer language.
   - Run smoke tests: simple text generation, streaming, and embeddings with provided test dataset (5–10 sample prompts).

5) Performance Baseline (owner: Performance Eng)
   - Capture baseline latency and throughput using canonical test harness (targets: p50 < 120ms for short prompts; 99th percentile target defined per plan).
   - Identify recommended model variant and quantization profile.

6) Go/No-Go Validation (owner: CSM)
   - Validate acceptance criteria: functional tests pass, SLO baseline reached, and security checklist complete.
   - Obtain written customer signoff and schedule production cutover.
integration_checklist:
- SDK & API compatibility
  - Provide language-specific SDK snippets (Python, Node) and sample env vars to set (REDWOOD_API_KEY).

- Rate limits and quotas
  - Confirm expected QPS and token rate; request quota increases for Dedicated customers via support channel.

- Model selection & configuration
  - Recommend model variant with notes: e.g., "redwood/model-ggml-1.2-8bit" for cost-sensitive workloads, "redwood/llama2-13b-opt" for high-quality chat.
  - Provide suggested batching and cache TTLs (default cache_ttl: 30s for prefix caching).

- Deployment types
  - Hosted: validate API endpoints and regional routing.
  - Dedicated: verify reserved capacity pool name and scaling policy.
  - Private: confirm on-prem package version and KMS integration (KMS provider: AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault).

- Example config snippet (customer-facing):
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_live_xxx
  REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
  MODEL=redwood/llama2-13b-opt

- Acceptance tests to include:
  1) Authentication test (200 OK, token validated).
  2) Latency test (p50/p95 thresholds).
  3) Functional test for streaming and function calling.
  4) Embeddings similarity sanity check (cosine_similarity > 0.8 for known pairs).
escalation_playbook:
Purpose: Provide a fast, consistent escalation path to minimize customer impact for Sev1/Sev2 incidents.

Severity definitions:
- Sev1 (P0): Production outage or data loss affecting >30% of customer traffic or blocking core feature.
- Sev2 (P1): Degraded service impacting significant functionality for a customer (<30% traffic but major feature impairment).
- Sev3 (P2): Minor customer-impacting issues or non-urgent bugs.

Escalation matrix (contact order):
1) Support Tier 1 (CS Support Queue) — initial triage, gather logs, reproduce.
2) Support Tier 2 (Platform SRE/CS Escalation) — deeper troubleshooting, log review, trace analysis.
3) Runtime Team (eng-serving-runtime on-call) — kernel/scheduler, batching, memory issues.
4) Infra / Cloud Ops (eng-infra on-call) — networking, capacity, cloud provider incidents.
5) Engineering Incident Lead & CSM Director — executive escalation and customer comms.

Immediate actions for Sev1 (ordered checklist):
1) Open incident in PagerDuty with tag: customer:{org} and sev:1.
2) Triage: collect request IDs, API keys used, region, model, and recent deploys/rollouts.
3) Apply mitigation: route traffic to fallback model/region or pause problematic routing rule.
4) If root cause is unknown after 30 minutes, schedule bridge (Zoom) and invite customer POC.
5) Communicate status updates every 15 minutes for first hour, then every 30 minutes until resolved.

Communication templates: include short status lines, apology, what we know, what we are doing, and ETA. Always include next update time.

Escalation SLAs (internal):
- Tier 1 ack: within 10 minutes.
- Tier 2 ack: within 30 minutes for Sev1.
- On-call eng response: within 15 minutes of Tier 2 escalation.

Post-incident: run postmortem within 72 hours, include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and rollback plan. Assign remediation tickets with owners and target dates.
known_issues_and_workarounds:
This section captures recurring issues observed during enterprise integrations. Each entry includes symptoms, root-cause (if known), and the currently recommended workaround.

1) Symptom: Intermittent 429s during traffic bursts.
   - Likely cause: client-side burst exceeding token-rate quota or batching limits.
   - Workaround: Implement client-side token throttle and exponential backoff; increase reserved concurrency or request quota via account team.

2) Symptom: Elevated p99 latency after model rollout.
   - Likely cause: new kernel scheduling differences or changed sequence-length distribution.
   - Workaround: Roll back to previous model variant, run perf harness to compare, then coordinate a canary rollout with reduced traffic.

3) Symptom: Private deployment failing at KMS unwrap step.
   - Likely cause: misconfigured key policy or network egress blocking KMS endpoints.
   - Workaround: Validate KMS key policy includes Redwood service principal; ensure outbound access to KMS endpoint or configure an on-prem HSM integration.

4) Symptom: Embeddings similarity drift vs baseline.
   - Likely cause: model variant mismatch or preprocessing change (tokenization differences).
   - Workaround: Confirm model artifact version and input normalization pipeline; re-run evaluation harness and pin model version.

5) Symptom: Streaming responses truncated for long prompts.
   - Likely cause: client-side timeout (reverse proxies) or server stream buffer limits.
   - Workaround: Increase client read timeout, verify proxy buffering headers (e.g., chunked transfer encoding), and set stream_keepalive config.
health_checks_and_qbr_template:
Quarterly Business Review (QBR) & Health Check template — use as the canonical slide/backing doc for enterprise customers.

Sections:
- Executive summary (1 slide): health snapshot, adoption KPIs, top wins, and asks.
- Operational health (metrics):
  - Uptime (30/90/365 day): target >= 99.9% for Dedicated customers.
  - Latency (p50/p95/p99) for primary routes (short prompts): target p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms (adjust per SLA tier).
  - Error rate: target < 0.5% 4xx/5xx combined.
  - Token consumption and cost per 1M tokens (trend vs prior quarter).
- Integration health:
  - Success rate of webhook callbacks, streaming session stability, and embedding similarity regressions.
- Incidents & reliability review:
  - Number of Sev1/Sev2 incidents, MTTR, and action items closed since last QBR.
- Roadmap alignment:
  - Upcoming feature launches, rollout windows, and potential impact on customer workloads.
- Recommendations & next steps:
  - Suggested model/quantization changes, batching tweaks, or Dedicated capacity adjustments.

Health check cadence & owners:
- Weekly automated health digest to customer (owner: CSM).
- Monthly technical health review with Solutions Eng for accounts above $50k/month.
- Quarterly QBR led by CSM with TAM and Solutions Eng.

Example KPI table (as text):
- Metric | Current | Target | Trend
- Uptime (30d) | 99.95% | 99.9% | +0.01
- p95 latency | 320ms | 350ms | -10%
- Error rate | 0.3% | 0.5% | stable
- Tokens / month | 12M | N/A | +23%

Recommended deliverables ahead of QBR:
1) Pre-QBR data pull and topline (CSM).
2) List of 3 operational wins and 3 open risks (Customer + CSM).
3) Technical appendix with traces and perf runs (Solutions Eng).
support_process_and_slas:
Support channels:
- Support portal (primary): support.redwood.ai (ticketing system)
- Slack: enterprise-customers workspace for customers with Slack integration (opt-in)
- PagerDuty: for Sev1 alerts (PD escalation policy: Redwood-Ent)

SLA summary (examples):
- Hosted Free/Tier: best-effort support, 24–48h response.
- Enterprise (paid): P1 (Sev1) initial response within 30 minutes, P2 within 4 hours, P3 within 1 business day.

Ticket lifecycle overview:
1) Ticket created in support portal with classification tags (severity, product-area, customer-tier).
2) Tier 1 triage: reproduce and collect logs; if unresolved escalate to Tier 2.
3) Tier 2 investigation with eng on-call; apply mitigations.
4) Resolution and customer confirmation; close ticket with summarized root cause and follow-up actions.

Escalation triggers to open a bridge:
- Multiple customers impacted with increased error rate across regions.
- Single enterprise customer facing data loss or production outage.
- Repeated regression after rolling deploy.

RCA / Post-incident expectations:
- Postmortem published to confluence within 72 hours for Sev1, including timeline, contributing factors, and action items.
- Owners assigned with due dates tracked in JIRA.
ownership_and_contact_matrix:
Primary owners:
- CSM (customer success) — overall customer relationship and QBR ownership.
- Solutions Engineering — integration, architecture, and go-live technical owner.
- Support Tier 1/2 — initial triage and operational troubleshooting.
- Runtime Team — model-serving runtime, kernel, and scheduling issues.
- Infra Team — cloud, networking, and capacity issues.

Contact points (examples):
- Customer Success general: cs-team@redwood.ai
- Enterprise support portal: support.redwood.ai
- On-call (runtime): runtime-oncall@redwood.ai (PagerDuty link: https://pagerduty.com/r/redwood-ent)

Rotation notes:
- On-call rotations live in /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-rotation.json. Ensure duty handovers are documented and runbook tasks completed before shift end.
